messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: p95 latency on /v1/generate > 800ms for last 5m (svc=hosted-api) :rotating_light:

maria (platform): seeing a support ticket — multiple customers reporting slow responses and timeouts. any quick visibility on cache hit/miss?

igor (eng-runtime): pulling metrics now. preliminary: prefix_cache_miss_rate spiked from ~8% -> ~62% at ~3187654000. KV eviction rate also up.

jen (support): customer-reported timestamps: 2026-03-17T14:25Z onwards. They saw p99s ~2.5s. provided curl repro but masked tokens.

sam (oncall): do we have a recent deploy around that time? canary rolled at ~3187653950 (rollout service:feature/prefix-normalize).

igor (eng-runtime): yes, feature/prefix-normalize went live 3187653920. I suspect key normalization logic introduced a subtle header-inclusion bug that adds ephemeral headers to prefix keys. seeing many unique prefix keys per user request.

maria (platform): example log snippet — look at the generated cache key fragments (trimmed):

```
prefix_key: gen:prefix:customer=acme:route=gen:headers=accept,authorization,traceparent
prefix_key: gen:prefix:customer=acme:route=gen:headers=accept,authorization,traceparent:fwd=1
prefix_key: gen:prefix:customer=acme:route=gen:headers=accept,authorization,traceparent:trace-id=abc123
```

maria (platform): trace-id and fwd bits should not be part of normalized prefix key. that explains cardinality explosion.

nidhi (sre): confirmed with queries — influx/metrics q:

```
SELECT percentile(value,95) FROM latency WHERE route='/v1/generate' GROUP BY time(1m)
```

result: p95 jumped from 120ms -> 950ms concurrent with prefix_cache_miss_rate jump.

sam (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback prefix-normalize canary 2) patch to strip ephemeral headers from keygen 3) increase cache entries temporarily 4) apply a short TTL for new keys to reduce steady-state churn.

igor (eng-runtime): quick, non-invasive hotfix I can push: change key builder to ignore headers matching regex `trace|trace-id|x-req|x-forwarded` and set a conservative TTL for newly-seen prefixes (30s) to avoid filling up. I can release to canary in ~10m.

maria (platform): for support: tell customers we're investigating and will roll a canary fix. tag affected customers for priority.

jen (support): done, updated tickets with ETA ~30m. customers appreciate transparency.

sam (oncall): if we need instant relief before fix lands, I can bump prefix cache max_entries on hot hosts. command (api-admin):

```
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://admin.internal/api/runtime/config -d '{"prefix_cache.max_entries": 4000000}'
```

(note: increases mem ~~ +18GB). Thoughts?

nidhi (sre): prefer not to blow memory. better to set ephemeral_key_ttl=30s and enable key-cardinality-rate-limit (new flag). I can flip these flags cluster-wide with minimal resource impact.

igor (eng-runtime): agree. I'll push key-strip + ephemeral_ttl change to canary immediately. if canary looks good for 10m, we roll. I'll attach quick smoke repro below.

maria (platform): repro steps for QA/support to validate fix (sanitized):

```
# baseline (before fix) - many unique keys
for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer x$i" -H "trace-id: t$i" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate > /dev/null
done
# inspect prefix key cardinality
redis-cli -n 2 SCARD prefix:gen:customer=acme
```

# after fix should show much lower cardinality for same loop
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer x$i" -H "trace-id: t$i" https://canary.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate > /dev/null
done
redis-cli -n 2 SCARD prefix:gen:customer=acme
```

jen (support): will run this against a replay dataset and report back.

sam (oncall): rolled key-cardinality-rate-limit=true on hot hosts and set ephemeral_key_ttl=30s (temporary). monitoring for p95 now.

ops-bot: RESOLVED ALERT: p95 on /v1/generate back to 160ms after mitigations (30m).

maria (platform): follow-ups: 1) patch PR to canonicalize header list and add unit tests (igor) 2) postmortem with customer impact summary (jen + nidhi) 3) conservative rollout plan for normalization with staged canaries and metrics gating.

igor (eng-runtime): opened PR #7892 with tests. adding assert to keygen that ephemeral headers are excluded. will request review.

nidhi (sre): creating incident ticket INC-2026-134 and will attach metric graphs + memory/cost impact note.

jen (support): customers updated, one asked for postmortem. capturing timeline.

sam (oncall): if anyone notices resurgence ping @oncall immediately. good run team. :cake:
